claims.claim: For many purposes Earth can be approximated as a sphere, but it more closely approximates an ellipsoid that is flattened at the poles and wider at the equator.
A geoid is an irregular reference surface related to mean sea level that extends conceptually through land, while an ellipsoid is a smooth mathematical approximation used for calculations.
Most of Earth's interior cannot be observed directly, so its structure is inferred from indirect observations; seismic measurements are one important source of evidence.
Measurements of Earth's shape, rotation, orientation, and gravity help refine knowledge of solid-Earth properties and processes.
An Earth-structure model is a testable representation matched to a purpose and available evidence; it is not a literal photograph of the whole planet.
